newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa aided by weak stg but selling continue.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa aided by weak stg but selling continue.

text.p: London cocoa futures were underpinned by sterling's weakness on Thursday morning but continued trade and origin selling erased early gains.
Traders said sterling's overnight losses against the dollar and European currencies prevented cocoa from slipping off.
"I am a little surprised," said one trader. "I was expecting a bit more manufacturer interest and a bit less origin price fixing."

Benchmark March position started the session three stg higher but retreated back to a midsession level of 873 stg, one down, after touching a session high of 879. Other forward contracts made gains of up to three stg with May up one at 898.
Turnover was 3,105 lots including structure trading which saw the key March/May spread widen an inch to 24 stg.
The pound clawed back some lost ground in European morning trading after an overnight sell-off which traders said was a correction after a rally.

It was pushed to a low of 2.6610 marks in Far Eastern trading from a 52-month high of 2.7240. Against the dollar, it firmed off its overnight low of $1.6190 against 1.6540 late on Wednesday, trading at $1.6325 at midday.
Traders described the sell-off as delayed reaction to weaker than expected December retail sales which dampened interest rate rise speculation.

In fundamental news, Ivorian industry sources pegged arrivals by January 20 at around 710,000-720,000 tonnes compared with 765,000 a year ago. They said a crop of over one million tonnes was looking increasingly likely.
There was no immediate reaction, but the latest arrivals figure look set to depress the market sentiment further.
Sellers in the physical market were struggling with lack of demand as Ivorian offers for February shipment at 25 stg under March met with no buyers.
"You just can't sell at 25 under," said one. "Either people have high priced contracts which they can't get out of, or they are expecting enourmous stocks to come onto the market soon."
Ghanaian cocoa for Jan-March shipment was trading at level with LIFFE March, traders said. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom 44-171-542 8072
